Title: Moody's cuts Botswana rating again as diamond slump weighs on economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Ratings agency Moody's on Friday downgraded Botswana's domestic- and foreign-currency long-term issuer ratings to "Baa2" from "Baa1", citing an expected deterioration in the country's public finances.
The move marks Botswana's second downgrade by Moody's in less than a year, leaving the sovereign just two notches above junk status.
It also comes days after Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe said Botswana expects a much smaller budget deficit in the current fiscal year, helped by higher-than-expected revenue from the central bank and measures to rein in spending.
Botswana's economy, long viewed as an African success story, has been hit hard by a prolonged downturn in the global diamond market, driven by economic uncertainty and the growing popularity of lab-grown diamonds. Diamonds typically account for about one-third of Botswana's national revenue and three-quarters of its foreign exchange earnings.
Moody's said weaker diamond-sector revenue, lower-than-expected receipts from the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), a key source of government income, and disappointing proceeds from newly introduced tax measures had weakened Botswana's fiscal position.
The rating agency also warned that it could cut again if Botswana were to materially increase its investment in De Beers through debt-financed transactions, a sale Anglo American is aiming to close in the final quarter of this year.
The outlook was changed to stable from negative, citing a stronger fiscal policy response and that a more sustained recovery in diamond revenue could slow the pace of debt accumulation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump says he does not want to 'integrate' with China on AI
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that despite a "big talk" this week with Chinese President Xi Jinping on AI, the US should not join efforts with China on the technology.
"We had a big talk on SI," Trump told reporters at the White House, using his preferred name of super intelligence.
"What they want to do is stop our progress because we're leading China by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way. We didn't spend that much time talking about it," he added.
Trump said he did not want to "integrate" AI initiatives with China because of US dominance.
"I would rather not integrate because we're leading by a lot," he said, adding: "When you're leading, you don't open it up to each other."

Title: US to finalise sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards
Article:
WASHINGTON: The Unites States Transportation Department on Monday will finalise sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards through 2031, reversing a push by the Biden administration ​to force automakers to build more electric vehicles, officials said on Saturday.
President Donald Trump said he had approved new fuel economy standards for cars and trucks, which he said will lower the price of new vehicles. "A major victory for America's auto workers is coming Monday," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.
The new standards would cut the cost of new vehicles but increase fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for decades, according to the department's own estimates.
Trump's push comes as American drivers are grappling with sharply higher fuel prices since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran at the end of February.
Under Democratic President Joe Biden, the government sought to push automakers to build more electric vehicles to meet rising fuel-efficiency standards. Biden increased required fuel efficiency for cars ‌by ⁠8.0 per cent annually for model years 2024 and 2025, 10 per cent for 2026 and 2.0 per cent annually from 2027 to 2031.
The Trump administration in December proposed retroactively revising down the 2022 model year fuel economy standard ​and then raising it between 0.25 per cent and 0.5 per cent annually through 2031.
The Transportation Department proposed a fleetwide average of 34.5 miles per gallon (14.7 km per litre) by ​2031, down from 50.4 miles per gallon (21.4 km per litre) under Biden. It estimated its proposal would cut average new ​vehicle costs by US$930 each.
But it would increase fuel consumption by ​around 100 ⁠billion gallons through 2050, fuel spending by US$185 billion and carbon dioxide emissions by about 5.0 per cent, the department said.
Trump's move will make it easier for automakers to sell consumers less efficient vehicles. "Lowering standards will accelerate what (Trump) has already been doing: handing the clean tech future to China and forcing Americans to pay more at the pump," said Pete Buttigieg, who headed the Transportation Department under Biden.
Biden focused on reducing US greenhouse gas emissions and fossil fuel use, accelerating a transition to clean energy and making the US. a global leader ​in clean-energy technology and manufacturing.

Title: Thousands march in Madrid over eviction of 87-year-old woman
Article:
MADRID: Thousands of people marched through Madrid on Saturday to protest the eviction earlier this week of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong home, calling for greater protection for tenants.
Images of Maricarmen Abascal being carried from her Madrid flat on a stretcher on Wednesday after police broke down her door have thrust Spain's housing crisis back into the spotlight ahead of a general election due in 2027.
Protesters rattled keys, blew whistles, chanted slogans and held banners calling for measures to curb rising housing costs and make evictions more difficult as they marched through central Madrid.
"You could be the next Maricarmen," read one banner.
Enrique Ortega de Miguel, a 38-year-old graphic designer who lives with his mother, said the housing market in Spain was "impossible."
"It is a struggle to find a place you can afford, then you live in fear of being forced out," he told AFP at the protest.
Government authorities put the turnout at around 25,000, while organisers of the protest said 300,000 participated.
"Maricarmen's eviction has caused outrage and marks a turning point," Alicia del Rio, spokesman for the Madrid Tenants' Union, told reporters at the start of the march which ended outside parliament.
Abascal, who has become a symbol of Spain's housing crisis, urged Spaniards to join the protest in a video message posted online just hours before it got underway.
"I want what has happened to me to serve so that it does not happen to other people," she said from hospital, where she has been treated for exhaustion since her eviction.
"I want it to encourage people to fight and to help change the laws that have allowed me to be evicted," she added in the video, posted by the tenants' union.
- 'Fed up' -
Abascal was forced to leave the apartment where she had lived for 70 years after a real estate firm acquired the property and raised the rent by 275 percent to 2,650 euros ($3,000), according to the union.
Irene Lopez, a 33-year-old engineer,  said the situation "has become unsustainable."
"There are people who can't afford to live in cities, rents are out of step with salaries," she told AFP, describing the eviction of Maricarmen as "the last straw."
Another protester, Maricarmen Arnedo, a 76-year-old pensioner, said while older people were being forced out of their homes, "young people can't move out of their parents' homes."
"We want house prices and rents to come down, because I'm fed up with washing the underpants of my 53-year-old son," she added.
- 'Social tragedy' -
Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who last year pledged to make housing a government priority, is under growing pressure to act. There have been regular protests across Spain since Abascal's eviction.
He has called Abascal's eviction a "social tragedy that we cannot accept."
The government is expected to approve a package of measures dubbed the "Maricarmen decree" at its next cabinet meeting, including the automatic renewal of rental contracts and further restrictions on evictions.
But it is unclear whether the package will be approved by parliament, where Sanchez's government lacks a majority.
While a similar bill was defeated earlier this year, Abascal's case has increased pressure on political parties to act.
The Bank of Spain estimates the country of around 50 million people is short of 700,000 homes, based on the gap between demand and new construction.
Spain has little public housing, while rents have been driven up by increased demand, including from tourism and population growth linked to immigration, analysts say.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit expected to trade range-bound next week ahead of key US data
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range against the US dollar next week as investors await key United States economic data for further clues on the direction of interest rates.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said attention would be on the US labour market next week, particularly the nonfarm payrolls report which is due to be released on Oct 2.
"We expect the ringgit to trade within a range of around RM4.07 to RM4.10 against the US dollar next week," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam said attention would also be on the US Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report due on Sept 30, with consensus estimates pointing to an inflation rate of 3.7 per cent in September, unchanged from August.
On the domestic front, he said focus would increasingly turn to Budget 2027, which is scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9.
"Domestic political developments could also influence how foreign investors assess the Malaysian market, with the Melaka state election among the developments being monitored," he said.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit increased against the greenback to 4.0715/0765 from 4.0795/0840 a week earlier.
The local currency also traded higher against a basket of major currencies during the week.
The ringgit appreciated versus the British pound to 5.3907/3973 from 5.4543/4603 on the previous Friday, gained against the Japanese yen to 2.5764/5797 from 2.5829/5860, and rose vis-a-vis the euro to 4.6378/6435 from 4.6849/6901.
It also traded mostly higher against Asean currencies.
The local note edged up versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1858/1900 from 3.1933/1971 a week earlier, strengthened vis-a-vis the Thai baht to 12.2036/2234 from 12.2383/2562, and climbed against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.4/227.8 from 229.7/230.0
However, it slipped against the Philippine peso to 6.52/6.53 from 6.50/6.51 last Friday.

Title: Bargain hunting seen on Bursa Malaysia next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia is expected to see bargain hunting next week, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) likely to trade within the 1,660-1,690 range, said an analyst.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said investors are expected to remain wary of the Malaysian market as elevated United States Treasury yields could continue to pressure regional fund flows, although the recent correction has brought selected blue-chip valuations to more attractive levels.
He said the market's direction would also depend on developments in global bond yields and investor risk appetite.
"With the FBM KLCI's relative strength index at around 35, near oversold territory, we expect bargain hunting to emerge in fundamentally strong heavyweights, particularly banks and defensive names, should external conditions stabilise.
"Nevertheless, 1,670 remains a key resistance level, which could cap the near-term recovery," he told Bernama.
Thong said attention would also turn to China's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and the US employment report, which could influence regional risk appetite and the direction of bond yields.
For the week ended yesterday, bargain hunting lifted the index early in the week, but gains were capped by elevated US Treasury yields, higher oil prices, geopolitical uncertainties and foreign selling.
The benchmark index ended marginally lower on Friday amid concerns over rising yields and escalating tensions in West Asia.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FBM KLCI increased 6.06 points to 1,671.62 at yesterday's close, from 1,665.56 a week earlier.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index rose 44.92 points to 12,456.64, the FBM Top 100 Index gained 33.09 points to 12,243.46, the FBM Emas Shariah Index shed 5.76 points to 12,306.23 and the FBM ACE Index expanded 288.26 points to 5,532.86, while the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 0.89 of a point to 17,844.91.
By sector, the Energy Index advanced 41.21 points to 861.83 and the Plantation Index erased 161.57 points to 9,334.87. The Industrial Products and Services Index slid 1.14 points to 184.1, while the Financial Services Index accumulated 137.86 points to 19,550.49.
Weekly turnover firmed to 17.11 billion units worth RM14.07 billion from 15.02 billion units worth RM14.18 billion in the previous week.
Main Market volume improved to 10.41 billion units valued at RM12.31 billion, from 9.38 billion units valued at RM12.93 billion previously.
Warrants turnover widened to 4.21 billion units worth RM661.61 million, from 3.61 billion units worth RM498.33 million in the previous week.
ACE Market volume garnered to 2.48 billion units valued at RM1.09 billion, compared with 2.02 billion units valued at RM748.59 million in the previous week.

Title: UNSC veto power must be challenged, abolished - Tok Mat
Article:
NEW YORK: Malaysia has stressed that the use of veto power at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) must be questioned and firmly challenged, particularly in cases involving crimes against humanity.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said global confidence in the world body's ability to act was now at its lowest point.
"No part of the UN is more in need of reform than the Security Council. And no part more clearly exposes the weaknesses of the UN than the Security Council," he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) here today.
Mohamad said Resolution 76/262 had established an accountability channel between the UNSC and the General Assembly.
"We must make full use of this resolution as a platform to strengthen accountability over the use of veto power. Expanding the Council's membership alone will not address its failures.
"The veto power must be challenged, and it is the veto power that must be abolished. We must begin that effort now," he said.
Mohamad said there was still time to save the global order, and that the paralysis of the UNSC should not mean the paralysis of the UN.
"It is fair to say that global confidence in the UN's ability to act is now at its lowest point. This situation is destroying confidence in the very idea of a multilateral order."
Mohamad said people were seeing the world order becoming increasingly fragmented, the resurgence of an arms race and hearing open threats to use nuclear weapons.
"They see their respective governments choosing not to regulate artificial intelligence (AI) and the various ways it is being misused, but instead giving it more power," he said.
Amid this state of turmoil, Mohamad said the only way to correct the course was to rebuild confidence in proactive governance and multilateralism.

Title: 4 men killed after car crashes into parked lorry in Sepanggar
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Four men were killed after the Perodua Viva car they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a five-tonne lorry parked on the road shoulder at Taman Jaya Diri, Jalan Sepanggar, early today.
The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call about the incident at 2.37am.
It said personnel from the Kota Kinabalu fire and rescue station, assisted by the Lintas fire and rescue station, arrived at the scene at 2.59am and found all four victims, whose identities are still being ascertained, trapped inside the vehicle.
"The firemen found that the accident involved a Perodua Viva which had skidded before crashing into a five-tonne lorry parked on the road shoulder.
"Four victims were trapped inside the vehicle, and the firemen used special rescue equipment to extricate them," it said in a statement.
The operation to extricate the victims was completed at 3.50am, with all four pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel.

Title: UN must move from reaction to prevention, especially in Gaza - Tok Mat
Article:
NEW YORK: The United Nations (UN) must move from reacting to crises to preventing them, with the task particularly urgent in Gaza, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said the UN should not merely respond after disasters had occurred by counting the dead, delivering supplies and rebuilding what had been destroyed, only to wait for the next crisis.
"This cannot be the future of multilateralism. We must move from reaction to prevention," he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st UN General Assembly on Saturday.
Mohamad said nowhere was that task more urgent than in Gaza.
He said Malaysia and many other member states had exhausted every effort in the pursuit of justice for Gaza, including consistently calling for an immediate ceasefire and unrestricted supply of aid.
"We have supported humanitarian work in Palestine. We have pushed for punitive action towards Israel. And we have advocated for full Palestinian membership in this Hall," he said.
However, he said the collective will of the General Assembly had repeatedly encountered the silencing effect of the veto.
"Malaysia will speak plainly: We are sick of it," he said.
He said Malaysia would continue to support efforts to strengthen the multilateral system and ensure that it could respond effectively to conflicts and humanitarian crises.
According to Gaza's Health Ministry, more than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 174,000 injured in Gaza since October 2023.
The foreign minister is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 for Malaysia's participation in the 81st session of the UN General Asesmbly (UNGA).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police to quiz former Negri Sembilan exco members
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is expected to record statements from the 10 Negri Sembilan executive councillors whose appointments were revoked.
Their statements will be taken in Seremban today.
"An officer from Bukit Aman will travel to Negri Sembilan tomorrow (today). The former exco members are prepared to cooperate," a source told FMT.
The source, however, refused to divulge details but did not deny the possibility that it was linked to the state's constitutional crisis.
The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has revoked the appointments of members of the state executive council after they were found to have
breached their oath of office
.
The impasse in the state has been ongoing since April, when the Undang Yang Empat proclaimed the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was reported to be among those who
signed the proclamation
, although he later claimed that he had done so under duress.
He maintained that the current
exco line-up
remains valid as the members were barred from entering the offices at Wisma Negeri last week.

Title: Death toll from Indonesia ferry sinking jumps to 64
Article:
JAKARTA: The death toll after a ferry sank in Indonesia's Java Sea almost two weeks ago has jumped to 64, an official said on Saturday, as rescuers extended the search for dozens still missing.
The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 213 passengers and 30 crew when it lost contact with its shipping company after departing from Indonesia's second largest city Surabaya on Java island, headed for Banjarmasin on Borneo.
"Out of 243 persons onboard, 172 have been evacuated, 108 survived, 64 died, and 71 are still being searched for," National Search and Rescue Agency official Yudhi Bramantyo told a news conference.
Rescuers recovered four bodies from the submerged ship on Saturday, while seven others were found along the shoreline, Yudhi said.
He added that the search operation would be extended a further seven days but will be evaluated every three days.
Search-and-rescue operations typically last for seven days in Indonesia, and authorities can extend them based on factors including an assessment that some of the victims could still be recovered.
Marine accidents regularly occur in Indonesia, a vast Southeast Asian archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are often the main reasons for disasters.

Title: 5.2-magnitude quake hits Papua New Guinea
Article:

Title: Building resilient padi farming to strengthen Malaysia's food security
Article:
STRENGTHENING the nation's food security involves not only producing more food, but also building a resilient domestic agricultural ecosystem that can sustain farmers and domestic supply over the long term.
In the padi fields of Kedah and Perlis, a partnership involving some 200 farmers is showing how stronger links between agriculture and domestic manufacturing can contribute to that effort.
Through the Nestle Paddy Club (NPC), farmers cultivate more than 600ha of padi.
Since 2012, 100 per cent of the white rice used in Nestle's Cerelac infant cereals, produced in Malaysia, has been sourced domestically.
The programme is expected to supply about 2,800 tonnes of rice this year.
Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the programme reflected the company's focus on ingredient quality and its partnership with Malaysia's farming communities.
"Cerelac is an important brand because it is part of the nutrition we provide for babies aged 6 to 12 months. We apply all necessary care and quality requirements to ensure only the best ingredients go into the product.
"Rice is an important ingredient. We are here in the rice bowl of Malaysia, so we are proud to be partners with the local authorities and farming community," he said.
Beyond securing high-quality domestically grown rice, the programme also supports farmers to improve the way they farm.
NPC farmers get agricultural inputs every planting season, alongside knowledge and training, technical guidance in the field and support to improve crop quality.
The programme connects the rice they produce to Nestle's domestic manufacturing value chain. Participating farmers have consistently recorded yields above the national average.
For participant Bahriza Rejab, aged 53, the programme has changed the way he manages his crops.
"I'm a full-time padi farmer and have been in the industry for 30 years... The rice we produce is used to make baby food, so we don't want to use chemical pesticides.
"Nestle provides us with organic products from the time we sow the seeds until harvest. I'm fortunate because it provides them for free. The company also guide us in managing our crops to ensure that the rice we produce meets the requirements for baby food."
Fellow NPC farmer Sabri Nayan, 59, said the programme has encouraged more environmentally conscious farming practices.
"When we work with Nestle, we are taught and guided to care for the environment. When we use pesticides, we do not use just any product.
"The vitamins they provide are of high quality, and the silica helps strengthen the roots and support healthy growth. When the stems are stronger, the plants are more resistant to disease, resulting in healthier padi crops."
FROM FARM RESILIENCE TO FOOD SECURITY
The focus is now shifting towards making farming more resilient.
Healthier soils, more efficient farming practices and stronger farmer capabilities can help sustain yields, reduce production risks and better withstand climate and cost pressures.
In turn, this supports a more dependable domestic food supply.
A regenerative agriculture project for NPC farmers commenced in June, focusing on improving soil health, using water more efficiently, optimising agricultural inputs and reducing greenhouse gas emissions from rice cultivation.
The programme is also promoting practices such as Semi-Aerobic Rice Intensification and alternate wetting and drying.
KEEPING THE VALUE CHAIN LOCAL
After harvest, rice produced by NPC farmers is processed locally through milling, quality testing and manufacturing.
The process includes mechanical drying, storage, de-husking and several stages of polishing.
Rice samples undergo contaminant testing, microbiological analysis and chemical analysis to ensure they meet stringent quality and food safety requirements for infant nutrition.
Traceability is maintained throughout the journey from farm to finished product.
For farmers, this creates a direct link between what is grown in the fields of Kedah and Perlis and a domestically manufactured food product, while helping to build a reliable domestic supply of a key agricultural ingredient.
Padi is also part of Nestle Malaysia's wider domestic agricultural sourcing efforts under its Farmer Connect initiatives, which extend to chilli, coffee and cocoa.
For the NPC farmers, the benefits are felt on the ground: better crops, stronger livelihoods and the ability to continue farming from one season to the next.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pope prays at Lourdes after huge Paris mass
Article:
LOURDES, France: Pope Leo XIV prayed for France on Saturday at its holy shrine in Lourdes, after riding along the Champs Elysees in the popemobile and holding an emotional open-air mass in front of hundreds of thousands of worshippers in Paris.
The leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics is on a four-day trip to France, a secular country with deep Catholic roots, on the first official papal visit there in nearly two decades.
In the southwestern pilgrimage town the US pontiff prayed at the Grotto of Massabielle, where Catholic tradition holds that the Virgin Mary appeared in 1858 to a peasant girl, later Saint Bernadette.
Months of ahead of a presidential election with the far-right surging and immigration high on the agenda, he prayed to the Virgin Mary to "obtain for France wise and generous leaders... eager to serve the common good."
"May they make her (France's) voice heard in promoting the defence of fundamental human rights and peace in the world, rejecting the mentality of war once and for all."
AFP reporters saw him perform the rituals observed by the many pilgrims to the cave: touching the rock, lighting a candle and drinking spring water.
On Sunday, Leo will meet privately with seven victims of clerical sex abuse. A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Church had abused about 330,000 people as minors in France, over seven decades.
GIANT PARIS MASS
In an earlier highlight of the visit's second day, the 71-year-old pope led enthusiastic worshippers in a mass at Paris's Place de la Concorde, where a giant white canopy had been erected to serve as a makeshift altar.
His prayers were accompanied by choral and organ music as the sun broke through the grey skies.
"It is truly good and pleasant when brothers and sisters come together and glorify the greatness of God," said Pope Leo, dressed in white liturgical vestments.
Some 800,000 people had gathered all the way beyond the Arc de Triomphe, the Vatican said.
"It's one time in history to see the pope," said Aline Riziki, 41, who was born in the Democratic Republic of Congo and has lived in France for 11 years.
"I dropped everything to come here and see him, to pray for peace in the east" of her homeland, wracked by conflict for decades, she said.
'IMPORTANT MOMENT'
Jeanne de Montagnac, 29, came with her husband and two-year-old girl, who was perched on his shoulders.
"We're happy that, even if she won't remember it, we're sharing this with her," she said, a small golden cross dangling over her jumper.
"It's an important moment for us to be surrounded by other people who also have faith."
The first US pontiff was visiting France seven months before voters choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron.
A number of presidential hopefuls were present, including far-right leader Marine Le Pen and centrist Edouard Philippe.
Macron did not attend the mass but was represented by his wife Brigitte. The president said in a message on X that France was "proud to welcome Pope Leo XIV and this monumental mass in the heart of Paris."
'DIGNITY AND PEACE'
Earlier in the day, the pope met migrants at Maison Bakhita, an association supporting refugees. Leo said it was "possible to encounter one another and to live together in dignity and peace."
He also stressed the "fundamental role of women in building a civilisation of love."
The association said the pope's visit sent a "message" ahead of the April-May election.
Leo was the third pope to visit Lourdes after Benedict XVI in 2008 and Jean-Paul II in 1983 and 2004.
Thousands of faithful watched his arrival at the site on giant screens.
The sanctuary, one of the most important Catholic holy sites in the world, receives some three million pilgrims each year. Catholics credit it with miraculous healings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump rejects Iran proposal for deal to reopen Hormuz
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Saturday rejected a truce deal proposed by Iran that Teheran said could have reopened the Strait of Hormuz to shipping within a week.
The waterway is key to the world's energy supply and is now central to the conflict between the US and Iran, which is at a stalemate after nearly seven months.
"I reject their proposal," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "They made a proposal but I've rejected it."
"They want to make a deal where they open the Strait immediately because they're losing so badly. They want to make a deal and I think that's fine. I like making a deal too."
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, who was on his way back to Teheran after attending the UN General Assembly in New York, told CBS News the proposal had been developed "in coordination" with supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, according to an excerpt from the video interview shared by Iranian media.
Iran's plan calls for a cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who met earlier in the week with Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff.
He said the conditions were the same as those laid out in a memorandum of understanding signed with the US earlier this year, which called for the release of frozen Iranian assets, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil and an end to the US naval blockade.
On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz. Pezeshkian told CBS that the "process will begin from the very day they accept it."
At the UN, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan complained that the "international community has been absent" and failing to live up to the responsibility to keep the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab al-Mandab open.
"The kingdom rejects any party's use of these vital passages as a tool for pressure, threat, or harm to the interests of states," he said, stressing the waterways' importance to global energy security.
His Russian counterpart, Sergei Lavrov, told member states that "Russia, together with other responsible states, stands ready to constructively contribute to stabilising this strategically important region."
In New York, Pezeshkian met with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, according to his office, and said: "Iran has not walked away from the negotiating table but, given past experiences, it no longer trusts the United States."
Araghchi said at the UN: "Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days."
"The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure," he added.
However, within hours of his comments The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump was skeptical that Teheran would meet his demands and expects to renew the US bombing campaign.
Trump also posted an image to his Truth Social platform of a map showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled "Trump Strait."
Hossein Mohebi, a spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards, was quoted by Tasnim news agency as saying: "We will not cease punishing the US until Iran's seven conditions are met."
Mohebi had told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday that ending hostilities in Yemen was also among Teheran's demands.
Washington and Teheran signed a memorandum of understanding in June that aimed to end the war, to reopen the strait and to launch talks on Iran's nuclear programme.
But the deal broke down shortly afterwards when Iran fired on commercial ships in Hormuz that it accused of deviating from its approved route through the waterway.
Iran requires ships to obtain authorisation before passage, citing security and sovereignty reasons.
Ships that refuse to comply are regularly targeted, while the United States sporadically bombs Iranian coastal areas in retaliation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Datuk V.L. Kandan: An educator to the very end [WATCH]
Article:
ON the morning of Sept 15, the ping of my mobile phone startled me awake as I tried to drift back to sleep after Subuh prayers. The message simply read: "Dear Zaharah, it is 6am in London now. But then, you Muslims are early birds! I haven't spoken with you in ages. May I call now? Kandan."
"Caaaan!" I replied, only to regret my informality almost immediately.
When you are communicating with Datuk V.L. Kandan, a product of the Kirkby Malayan Teachers' Training College (MTTC), an educator, a veteran lawyer, and much more, you do not take liberties with your spelling.
There was no time for a mental slap on the wrist. My phone sprang to life again, and I was delighted to hear his voice on the other end of the line; cheerful, though punctuated by bouts of coughing during our seven-minute conversation.
"I am 89, Zaharah, and I have been poorly," he said, explaining the coughs.
After promising to share more stories, we said our goodbyes. It was the last call I would receive from Kandan. It was to be his last call to anyone.
Six days later, I received another WhatsApp message from his number. It was from his daughter, Shakuntala, informing me that her father had died at 2pm on the same day he had called me, barely 40 minutes after our conversation ended.
I was shocked beyond words.
The educator in him remained present until his very last breath. He had wanted to tell me how proud he was of his grandnephew's academic achievements, and he wanted to speak about the importance of education in shaping a person's life.
That final phone call, and the story he was so eager to share, was in itself a testament to what Kandan was all about: an unwavering passion for education.
Even in the final minutes of his life, he was not speaking about his own achievements, whether as a former assemblyman or as a distinguished lawyer with Shearn Delamore & Co, where he earned a reputation as a leading intellectual property practitioner.
No, he wanted to speak about a young person's educational journey, encouraging others, and reminding us of the transformative power of learning. In that sense, Kandan remained an educator to the very end.
[[nid:1541833]]
I had met Kandan twice, once in 2017 and again in 2019, when he and other Kirkbyites, all in their late 80s, attended their organised reunions at their alma mater in Kirkby.
Kandan was from the fifth batch of teachers despatched to Kirkby to a place he repeated and proudly announced as "the one and only teachers' training college in the world, to be set up in a foreign land, to train teachers for a country that was yet to attain independence. It was not only unprecedented, it was phenomenal!"
The first batch of 149 Malayans arrived on the Blue Funnel in 1952. Three years later, Kandan and the fifth batch arrived on the BOAC Arganout.
When I met the group at the Liverpool train station in August 2017, it was like meeting a group of schoolchildren on their first outing; excitement and nostalgia etched on their faces. Kandan and several others wore blazers proudly displaying the Kirkby training college emblem, exchanging shared experiences of yesteryear.
It was a historic gathering in Granborne Chase, the site of their alma mater, to unveil a plaque honouring the spot where, on Feb 7, 1956, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj announced the date of the country's independence to about 300 students of the MTTC — a site in North West England that is now a piece of Malaysia's history.
Kandan and his fellow Kirkbyites were among the first to hear the historic announcement after Tunku and his delegation returned from the successful negotiations at Lancaster House.
This was a story, among others, that Kandan proudly and repeatedly narrated to his family.
"The plaque was not simply about remembering where Kirkby once stood, but about remembering what Kirkby stood for and carrying that spirit forward," said Renuka, Kandan's second daughter.
It was Renuka who took Kandan to Kirkby as his 78th birthday treat in 2015. It was during this visit that he went to a grocery store he frequented in the 1950s and found a card appealing for information on the Kirkby Teachers' Training college. Kandan then made his way to the Knowsley Resource Centre —and the rest is history.
"I think my father's lifelong commitment to education can be traced back to his beginnings as a teacher. Although he eventually left the classroom to pursue a career in law, I don't think he ever stopped thinking of himself as an educator.
"Kirkby and his early teaching years instilled in him a belief that education was one of the most powerful ways of changing a young person's life and, through them, the future of the country," said Renuka, who now lives in Brighton.
Among the tributes for the late Kandan was a story from someone whose life was significantly impacted by his passion for education. Sumiita Devi Panirselvan, a former student of SJKT Ladang Raja Musa, Kuala Selangor, had scored 7A's in her UPSR examination, making her the first student in her school to achieve that milestone.
In a touching tribute, she wrote about Kandan's visit to the estate.
"He made a solemn promise to support any student from SJKT Ladang Raja Musa who achieved outstanding results, and he kept that promise.
"For a child growing up in Raja Musa Estate, meeting a leader of his stature was a profound and unforgettable moment.
"His visit did more than simply celebrate my academic achievement; it gave me a new sense of confidence and instilled in me a lasting determination to excel in my higher education", wrote Sumiita, an engineering geologist.
Kandan's impact, she said, extended far beyond her own life.
"His presence and financial support inspired the entire community, proving to the children of the estate that their dreams were within reach. He passionately believed that the younger generation could uplift themselves and transform their lives through education."
I wish Kandan had shared this story with me, but the man hailed as a gentle giant wasn't one to speak about his achievements.
"Serendipity" was one of his favourite words, Renuka recalled.
Indeed, his discovery of that small postcard in a village grocery store window, which eventually brought him and his fellow Kirkbyites back to the place he called his Camelot, seemed an act of serendipity.
So too, perhaps, was the final phone call he made to me that morning, a last conversation that perfectly reflected the values by which he lived: education, encouragement and hope for the next generation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Country cannot tolerate corruption, plundering of national wealth, says Anwar
Article:
BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government respects the Federal Constitution and the decision of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong regarding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's case.
He said this did not prevent him from offering views and advice based on jurisprudence, the law and the nation's interests.
He said the government's position was clear that the country could not tolerate corruption or the act of taking national wealth for personal gain.
"When we discuss the controversy surrounding Najib's case, I abide by the spirit of the Federal Constitution, but this does not prevent a prime minister from giving views and advice based on jurisprudence and the law.
"What do we want to convey? This country cannot tolerate corruption and the practice of plundering national wealth," he said at the 3 Generations Appreciation Dinner: Continuing the Legacy of the Struggle here today.
Anwar also referred to several issues involving institutions that had previously drawn public attention, including Lembaga Tabung Haji, the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), while saying those responsible for taking the nation's wealth must bear full responsibility.
"Tabung Haji, Felda, 1MDB, people who plundered wealth must answer for it. So whatever the decision, it should not deviate from saving our country," he said.
Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, after being convicted of misappropriating RM42 million in SRC International Sdn Bhd funds.
On Sept 18, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, granted Najib a conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine and compliance with the conditions imposed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nation will be crippled if driven by anger, says Anwar
Article:
BANGI: A country will be crippled if driven by anger, but must instead be guided by knowledge, which forms the foundation of its strength, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the strength of any struggle could not depend solely on spirit and emotion, but must instead be supported by knowledge capable of raising public awareness and instilling a sense of responsibility.
"My friend, the late Ustaz Fadzil Noor, reminded us that the Islamic cause does not rise solely through an outpouring of spirit, emotion and sentiment, but through the strength of knowledge that raises awareness and instils a sense of responsibility.
"And now, for example, when discussing the Madani nation, it must be strengthened with knowledge. This is what lays the foundation for building a strong nation," he said at the 3 Generations Appreciation Dinner: Continuing the Legacy of the Struggle, here today.
Also present were his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.

Title: Proton Iswara steals the show in Apple's iPhone 18 Pro promo [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The appearance of a Proton Iswara in Apple's promotional video for the iPhone 18 Pro has caught the attention of social media users in Malaysia.
The national car model, introduced more than 3 decades ago, features in a chase scene in which a group of young people use the vehicle to escape from a mysterious man.
The 58-second video was uploaded by Apple on Sept 23 as part of its #ShotoniPhone18Pro campaign to showcase the smartphone's camera capabilities.
What caught attention was that the entire sequence was filmed in a single continuous shot, without cuts, including a scene of the actors running towards the Proton Iswara before driving away.
The appearance of the car was quickly spotted by Malaysian social media users, with Apple's comment section filled with reactions such as "I saw Proton Saga there", "Wait, is that Malaysia Proton car?" and "Proud to be a Malaysian."

A post shared by apple (@apple)
Some users also joked about the appearance of the national car, leaving comments such as "Malaysia mendunia (goes global)" and "I saw Proton, I press LIKE."
The video was directed by British cinematographer Matt Lewis, who was also involved in the production of Netflix series Adolescence.
Lewis used a continuous one-shot technique for the chase sequence, while making use of the iPhone 18 Pro's camera features to create focus transitions as the camera moved.
The Proton Iswara was introduced in 1992 as an updated version of the Saga Megavalve and was previously exported to the United Kingdom.
In the UK market, the model was known as the Proton Mpi.

Title: Militant attack kills 11 at security check post in northern Pakistan
Article:
PESHAWAR: Militants rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into a security check post in northern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people and wounding 18 others, police and rescue officials said Saturday.
Saifullah Khan, a Dera Ismail Khan police official, told AFP that the attack on the security check post – which is jointly operated by police, military and customs personnel – took place "around noon."
"A suspected suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the checkpoint, killing 11 people," he said.
Bilal Faizi from the 1122 rescue services told AFP that they had recovered eleven bodies following "the militant attack", adding that 18 others were wounded in the incident.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack.
Earlier this month, at least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, were killed in an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province.
Pakistan has blamed the increase in attacks in KP and the southern border province of Balochistan on militancy emanating from Afghanistan, where the Taliban government denies Afghan involvement.
The accusations have sparked a bitter rift and armed conflict between the neighbouring countries, and Pakistan has carried out deadly airstrikes it says target militants on Afghan soil. — AFP

Title: Teen's hand trapped in meat grinder at Ipoh premises
Article:
IPOH: A 19-year-old Orang Asli teenager was injured after his right hand became trapped in a meat grinder at a premises in the Bercham 10 Light Industrial Area here today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received a distress call at 4.41pm.
He said eight personnel from the Ipoh Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the location to rescue the teenager.
"When the team arrived, the victim's right hand was still trapped in the meat grinder, but he was conscious.
"The operation commander then requested assistance from Health Ministry medical personnel at the scene to administer anaesthesia to the victim's hand as he was in pain during the rescue operation," he said here today.
Sabarodzi said the rescue operation was carried out using the Saver concept, with firefighters separating and cutting parts of the machine using specialised equipment.
"The cutting work continued until the grinder's blade mould, but the victim's right hand could not be freed as the blade mould was made of stainless steel.
"As the victim's condition weakened, the rescue operation was stopped and discussions were held with the medical team," he said..
The teenager was later taken to Raja Permaisuri Bainun Hospital for further treatment.

Title: 'As many as it takes': Peepal Baba's half-century mission to reforest India
Article:
WITH Delhi's choking haze hanging overhead, Peepal Baba presses a young tree into the earth, continuing a nearly half-century mission to restore India's vanishing green cover.
"When I was young, I planted saplings like a soldier," said Swami Prem Parivartan, better known as "Peepal Baba", or "tree father", rubbing earth between his fingers and mixing wet mulch around the sapling's base.
It is the latest tree among millions that his teams estimate to have planted.
"What started as a solitary act of planting became contagious," he said.
At 60, he has turned a childhood fascination with trees into one of India's largest grassroots planting movements.
"We did not wait for governments to act," he said. "We gathered friends, volunteers, wanderers, believers."
In Delhi, a sprawling megacity of 30 million people with scorching summers and toxic winter air, his answer to environmental despair is stubbornly simple — plant a tree, keep it alive, then plant another.
"Whatever little we can do for the environment, we have to do," he said, beaming a warm smile.
Exactly how many trees he has planted, and how much land has been restored, are not his focus.
His trust estimates it has restored vegetation across more than 270,000ha, or 2,700 sq km — more than twice the size of Delhi and nearly as large as California's Yosemite National Park.
The organisation says it has planted or preserved 26 million trees.
But he insists numbers and exact areas are not the point.
"I never counted shade in digits," he said. "It is not about planting one tree or two trees or 1,000 trees. It's about how you manage the land on which those plants have been planted."
His fascination with trees was nurtured by his grandmother and a garden he loved tending.
He planted his first trees on his 11th birthday, including a peepal, or Ficus religiosa, a tree with vast spreading roots, sacred to several of India's religions.
Peepal trees have provided shade for village meetings, temples, tea stalls and markets for centuries.
He calls them "cooling towers of human hope" in his 2026 autobiography.
He put aside a career in academia after university.
Instead, he set off across India by scooter to encourage people to grow trees — and his nickname came from a villager he met while planting.
"Peepal Baba", he decided, carried more authority than "environmentalist", which he regarded as a foreign-sounding word at the time.
"My nickname travelled faster than my scooter," he writes.
That scooter carried him across India multiple times.
From his notebooks, he estimates he travelled nearly 540,000km — enough to circle the Earth more than 13 times.
He slept wherever he found shelter —in temples, homes, bus shelters or beneath a peepal tree.
Long sustained by individual and community donations, the trust has in recent years also brought on major corporate donors to expand its work.
With more than 1.6 million Instagram followers, he now also spreads his message through social media and a growing network of volunteers in the field.
His philosophy has expanded from planting trees to restoring the soil that sustains them.
"Every civilisation that respected its soil prospered; everyone that ignored it perished," he said.
"We've built skyscrapers tall enough to touch clouds, but forgotten how to kneel and touch the soil."
For him, the task remains simple: plant a tree, care for it and make sure it survives.
"When people ask, 'How many?', I answer, 'As many as it takes to give the Earth a second chance'."
The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump's diplomatic week lays bare the limits of his power
Article:
FROM his high-profile address at the United Nations General Assembly to his high-stakes White House summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, United States President Donald Trump this week was looking to reassert himself on the world stage.
But Trump's diplomatic flurry has done little to dispel the view among many analysts of a president beset by problems at home and abroad.
Trump has begun facing pushback from world leaders on issues ranging from the crisis in the Middle East to Russia's war in Ukraine, leaving the impression of a foreign policy agenda that has stalled.
This comes as Trump's Republican Party faces midterm elections in November that could further constrain him politically.
Even so, Trump's speech to the UN on Tuesday was a stark reminder of how he has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped to create from the ashes of World War 2.
Standing atop the rostrum of a world body dedicated to peacemaking, he issued a fresh threat to "annihilate" Iran if it did not agree to a deal, defended his coercive approach to Opec member Venezuela and signalled he may not be done deploying the US military to achieve his international aims.
Despite that strident stance, Trump's talks with Xi on Thursday put the US president up against a Chinese counterpart who appeared to be in stronger position.
Xi's state visit was heavy on pomp and ceremony but light on substance, despite a host of thorny issues such as artificial intelligence, trade, Taiwan and Iran.
The most tangible outcome appeared limited to a two-month extension of a trade truce.
"Trump sees himself taking us back to a world where might makes right," said Brett Bruen, who was a foreign policy adviser in the Obama administration.
"It's noteworthy that he goes all wobbly when it comes to Xi Jinping and ascendant Chinese power."
A White House official said Trump's UN remarks "highlighted his various wins in advancing US interests around the world", including preventing Iran from getting a nuclear weapon.
The war with Iran, which Trump started alongside Israel on Feb 28, has dragged on for nearly seven months, disrupting global energy supplies and spreading to other countries in the region.
Iran's defiance has become the most intractable foreign policy challenge of Trump's second term.
Trump used his address at the UN to defend his attack on Iran and to declare that "America is back", stronger than ever.
But after a string of early foreign policy achievements, including a Gaza ceasefire and the capture of Venezuela's leader, Trump's record in his second term in office is increasingly defined by stalemates.
World leaders appear to be preparing for a time when the US president's influence could begin to wane following the midterms, and with less than two-and-a-half years left in office.
Most European and Asian allies have already spurned Trump's demands for assistance in an Iran conflict he launched without consulting them.
At this year's UN gathering, some US partners took aim at Trump, mostly without mentioning him by name.
France's President Emmanuel Macron warned against a global "return to the law of the jungle".
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva decried foreign interference in his country's election next month and insisted that "we do not need aircraft carriers patrolling our waters, we need cooperation to stem the flow of weapons and money that fuel crime".
In another sign of diminished clout, Trump's effort to pressure Ukraine and Russia to agree to even a limited energy ceasefire failed to gain much traction.
And while Trump touted a deal with Denmark and Greenland for an expanded US military presence in the vast Arctic island, it fell short of his initial demand to "own" the territory by force.
"A year ago, few countries dared cross Trump," Ian Bremmer, president of the Eurasia Group, wrote on X. "Now Canada, Europe, China, Iran, Russia and others are all more willing to say no."
At one point, Trump himself seemed to wonder how much international sway he actually possessed.
In his speech, he told world leaders he wanted to rebrand AI as "super intelligence".
"Let's see if I have any power," he said. "Maybe I do and maybe I don't. We're going to find out pretty soon."
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Shared patterns of persecution make Rohingya and Gaza two sides of same coin
Article:
For decades, the world's conscientious majority, Malaysia included, have condemned and sanctioned Israel's occupation, bombing and genocide of Palestine. Yet,  similar  persecution is occurring in Malaysia's regional backyard: Myanmar's annihilation and displacement of the Rohingya.
This stateless Muslim minority populate Myanmar's Rakhine state, on the country's northwestern coast bordering Bangladesh.
Rohingya and Palestinians share uncanny patterns of persecution and state-sanctioned aggression, contrasted only by historical and political circumstances.
The two groups face severe, systemic crises of massive displacement, widespread destruction of homes and strict restrictions on movement.
Both are devoid of state sovereignty and citizenship,  attracting critical international scrutiny.
The outcome is international legal action on alleged genocide and human rights violations before the International Court of Justice.
Still, there are differences: the persecution of the Rohingya is ethnic and citizenship-based on a minority within Myanmar.   The 2017 military campaign leading to mass killings and village destruction forced 700,000 Rohingya to seek refuge in Bangladesh.   On the flip side, the Palestinian
nakbah
is intertwined with national conflict over territory, sovereignty, occupation, security and competing claims to self-determination.
Plus, the Palestinian
nakbah
has geographical dimensions, encompassing Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem, Palestinian refugees and Palestinians who are citizens of Israel.
Yet, the  outcome is the same: human suffering, violence, and killings stemming from military interventions.
In Rohingya, the Myanmar military and the Arakan Army are responsible while Israeli state and military actions are central to the Palestinian occupation, displacement and genocide.
While Malaysia has assisted Palestinians through foreign aid and international backing, the Rohingya situation squarely hits home.
Now, Malaysia has called for more global backing to support countries hosting Rohingya refugees.   Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, in outlining the call in New York, implored for a sustainable solution, including pressing Myanmar to implement the Asean Five-Point Consensus.
He articulated that international assistance to host countries is pertinent, but a sustainable solution must address the root causes of displacement.   This means resolving citizenship purgatory and formalising conditions for refugees to return safely, voluntarily and with dignity to Rakhine.
Yet, the broader question would be: how long can the crisis be defined as a refugee problem when its basic antagonism remains?      Malaysia and fellow host nations cannot bear indefinitely the financial, humanitarian and social responsibilities of the Rohingya crisis.
In their immediacy, the Rohingya and Palestinians' crises are two sides of the same coin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kamaruddin will 'continue exco duties unless instructed otherwise'
Article:
KOTA BARU: Kelantan Bersatu chairman Datuk Kamaruddin Md Nor said he would leave any decision on his position as a state executive councillor to the state government amid a dispute between Bersatu and Perikatan Nasional (PN).
The dispute resulted in the suspension of PN activities effective Wednesday.
Kamaruddin, who is also the state executive councillor for tourism, culture, arts and heritage, said he would continue carrying out his duties as usual unless instructed otherwise by Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
"So far, I have not heard of any changes. The appointment of Exco members is the menteri besar's prerogative and depends on his discretion. What happens next is beyond my authority.
"In Kelantan, I am the only Exco member from Bersatu," said the Ayer Lanas assemblyman.
Earlier, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reminded Bersatu that the party is part of the state administrations in Kelantan, Kedah and Terengganu, all led by Pas.
It was reported that the Registrar of Societies (RoS) issued an order suspending all PN activities after issuing a notice to the coalition seeking an explanation over a complaint lodged by Bersatu.
RoS said the suspension was made under subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 (Act 832), following the notice issued to PN on Sept 22.
However, the department stressed that the notice was
not a decision to cancel
PN's registration, but was issued to give the coalition a reasonable period to respond to the complaint.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cockroaches, rat droppings: Two popular Sungai Besar eateries ordered shut for 14 days
Article:
SABAK BERNAM: Two popular food premises in Sungai Besar were ordered closed for 14 days after inspectors found various hygiene offences during Ops Bersih Premis Makanan yesterday.
The operation, held in conjunction with the district-level Hari Cuci Malaysia, also saw nine compounds issued against three premises inspected.
Among the offences found were cockroaches and rat droppings beside a kitchen refrigerator, dirty drains and an unhygienic chicken-cutting area.
Sabak Bernam District Council (MDSB), in a statement, said the operation was carried out by its Health and Environment Services Department and Enforcement Department from 9.30am.
"Two premises were ordered closed for 14 days under the Food Establishment By-Laws (Sabak Bernam District Council) 2007.
"The action was taken to ensure food premises remain clean and safe for customers and operators," it said.
MDSB said it would continue conducting regular inspections and monitoring of food premises to ensure hygiene and food safety standards were complied with.
The public is also encouraged to lodge complaints with MDSB if they find food premises operating in unhygienic or unsafe conditions.
Similar operations will continue from time to time to safeguard public health and hygiene standards.

Title: 'I have no information,' Tuan Ibrahim on BN talks
Article:
