Title: Six dead after explosion destroys building in Athens
Article:
ATHENS: Six people have died, the Greek fire brigade said on Saturday, after a two-storey residential building in a tourist area of central Athens collapsed following an explosion which the capital's mayor said was likely linked to gas infrastructure.
Emergency crews in heavy gear and red helmets assisted by rescue dogs, cameras and sensors found the bodies of six people, fire brigade spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis said in a televised briefing. They were looking for an elderly couple who lived in one apartment and four tourists who were staying in another as they removed debris from the building.
The fire brigade's crime investigation unit was also on site to identify the cause of the blast after reports of a gas smell in an area which is home to hotels and short-term rentals.
The tourists, two American couples, had been expected to check in to catch a flight from Athens airport at 3pm local time on Friday but did not show up, a police source said.
Ambulances stood by on Saturday to take the bodies to the hospital for identification.
Friday's blast destroyed the building in Plaka, near some of Athens' most visited sites including the Acropolis and the Temple of Zeus, damaging nearby houses, shops and cars and sending rubble and broken glass as far as three blocks away.
The building was reduced to twisted metal, shattered tiles and concrete, strewn with household items and clothing. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negeri Sembilan police say hostel tragedy linked to Form Four student ‘punishing’ junior  for breaking rules
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 27 — Police yesterday confirmed that preliminary investigations into the death of a Form Two student at a school in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, suggest the incident stemmed from the victim’s alleged breach of school rules.
Following this, the suspect — a Form Four student — is believed to have reprimanded and “punished” the younger boy over the offence.
According to
Astro Awani
, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the suspect has been remanded for six days beginning Saturday to assist investigations, after the application was filed at the Seremban Magistrates’ Court.
“So far, only one individual — the Form Four student — has been detained to help with the probe,” he told
Awani
.
It was reported earlier that the student was found unconscious at the school hostel Friday night and was taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
The Education Ministry has also ordered an immediate audit of the school following the boy’s death and said it would cooperate fully with police.

Title: ‘Hari Cuci Malaysia’ sets two new records with 272,390 people, 89 tonnes of recyclables
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Hari Cuci Malaysia (HCM) 2026 set two new records in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) yesterday through large-scale public mobilisation and recyclable material collection in a single day.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said in a statement that the two records were set with 272,390 people nationwide participating in HCM 2026 and the collection of 89,221.22 kilogrammes of recyclable materials in one day.
In addition, HCM 2026, conducted simultaneously across 469 locations nationwide, collected 8,010.19 tonnes of solid waste through cleaning activities and gotong-royong initiatives.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said in the statement that achieving the two records was not merely a success for KPKT but an achievement of all Malaysians who joined hands to realise the nation’s cleanliness agenda.
“The two records we created today are not just about numbers. Behind these figures are hundreds of thousands of Malaysians who came together, cleaned their surroundings, and recycled for a cleaner and more sustainable country,” he said.
He said the achievement showed that the spirit of gotong-royong remains strong within the community and has strong potential to translate into long-lasting behavioural change.
Nga added that HCM 2026 received support from 10,000 schools nationwide, with student participation recognised under the Physical Activity, Sports and Co-curricular Assessment.
He emphasised that involving the younger generation is vital to cultivating awareness that cleanliness, waste separation, and recycling habits must start at school age.
He said the success of HCM 2026, which brought together people from various backgrounds alongside government agencies, local authorities, the private sector, non-governmental organisations, educational institutions, volunteers, and local communities, should serve as a launchpad for greater efforts to strengthen the circular economy and sustainable solid waste management.
Nga said the event also should not end as a one-day programme.
“Records can be set in a day, but building a culture takes time.
“Our challenge moving forward is to ensure that the spirit of HCM 2026 translates into daily practice, do not litter, reduce waste, and make recycling a way of life,” he said.
In 2024, HCM set three MBOR records, including the highest simultaneous participation with 58,007 people, a waste collection of 4,645 tonnes in a single day, and non-stop operations running from 8 am to 8 pm. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials KPKT stand for Kementerian Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan.

Title: Teen worker’s hand trapped in meat grinder at Ipoh chicken factory
Article:
IPOH, Sept 27 — An Orang Asli man suffered injuries after his right hand became trapped in a meat grinder during an incident at a chicken processing factory in Bercham Light Industrial Area here today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team of personnel from the Ipoh Fire and Rescue Station was rushed to the scene after receiving a distress call at 4:41 pm.
“The incident involved a 19-year-old worker whose right hand was trapped in a meat grinder. Upon arrival, the fire engine crew found that the victim’s hand was still inside the machine and the victim remained conscious.
“The operation commander requested assistance from the Ministry of Health (MOH) medical team at the location to sedate the victim’s hand as the man was experiencing pain while the operation was being carried out,” he said in a statement today.
He added that the fire department used special cutter-spreader equipment to cut through the meat grinder down to the blade mold section, but the victim’s right hand could not be extricated because the blade mold was made of stainless steel and the victim’s condition was growing weaker.
He stated that after discussions with the MOH team, the victim was rushed to Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun for further treatment by the hospital. — Bernama

Title: MM2H brings in RM8.85b in economic value in less than two years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — The Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) programme generated RM8.85 billion in economic value between Oct 1, 2024 and Aug 31, 2026, including more than RM5 billion in property purchases and RM3.82 billion in fixed deposits.
Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the programme received 7,650 new applications during the same period across the Platinum, Gold, Silver and Special Economic Zone categories.
“MM2H has shown immense potential in expanding Malaysia’s foreign direct investment. The programme has successfully brought in billions of ringgit into the country in a short period of time and has benefitted many sectors of our economy,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Chiew said China led the applications with 3,847, followed by Taiwan (1,054), Hong Kong (324), Singapore (287) and the United States (284).
To further expand the programme’s reach to key target markets such as Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea, the MM2H One Stop Centre will organise overseas sales missions to these regions.
Chiew also said he had met key MM2H industry players and stakeholders, including consultants, real estate, education, healthcare and banking specialists, at the 14th MM2H National Workshop 2026 organised by the Malaysia My Second Home Consultants Association yesterday to gather feedback.
“Every concern is taken note of, and the ministry works closely together with other ministries and agencies for practical solutions,” he said, reiterating the ministry’s commitment to regulatory compliance, transparency and integrity to maintain the programme’s global reputation. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Knowledge, not anger, must drive the nation forward
Article:
BANGI, Sept 27 — A country will be crippled if driven by anger, but must instead be guided by knowledge, which forms the foundation for its strength, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the strength of any struggle could not depend solely on spirit and emotion, but must instead be supported by the strength of knowledge capable of raising public awareness and instilling a sense of responsibility.
“My friend, the late Ustaz Fadzil Noor, reminded us that the Islamic cause does not rise solely through an outpouring of spirit, emotion and sentiment, but through the strength of knowledge that raises awareness and instils a sense of responsibility.
“And now, for example, when discussing the Madani nation, it must be strengthened with knowledge. This is what lays the foundation for building a strong nation,” he said when speaking at the 3 Generations Appreciation Dinner: Continuing the Legacy of the Struggle, here yesterday.
Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
The event brought together more than 2,000 members of the Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement, Persatuan Wadah Pencerdasan Umat Malaysia and National Union of Malaysian Muslim Students.
The Prime Minister said that in the context of building a Madani nation, change must be based on conviction, idealism and noble aspirations to elevate the dignity of the people and the country, rather than a sense of supremacy, racism or incitement.
Anwar said society also needed to have a strong understanding of religion and faith, as being born a Muslim did not necessarily guarantee an understanding of Islam.
“Being born a Muslim and of Muslim descent does not guarantee understanding. Islamic movements, Islamic associations and Islamic organisations may emerge, but they do not necessarily guarantee the revival of the spirit of Islam beyond enthusiasm and the play of words... that is why our great responsibility is to revive the tradition of knowledge,” he said.
Anwar said his experience in the Islamic movement had also taught him that a struggle must be built on conviction and the belief to take action, rather than merely on the amount of support, votes or acceptance on social media.
“Because the ultimate consideration is to seek and obtain the blessings and pleasure of Allah SWT. And hopefully, with your spirit, strength and support, we can continue to build the strength of the Muslim ummah,” he said.
Anwar also stressed the importance of the tradition of knowledge, usrah and efforts to bring together new ideas in shaping public understanding, particularly in a country with diverse ethnicities and religions.
He said efforts to build the country must also give attention to education and mastery of new knowledge, including artificial intelligence (AI), while at the same time not neglecting fundamentals such as faith and morality.
“We must embrace new knowledge, AI, but if we reach for the sky while leaving our roots in the ground, we will certainly see weaknesses in the formation of the Negara-Bangsa (Nation-State),” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kids under 14 make up more than a third of Kelantan’s drowning deaths since 2023
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — Children under 14 accounted for about 36 per cent of the 96 drowning deaths recorded in Kelantan since 2023, highlighting the urgent need to strengthen preventive measures and water safety awareness for this group.
Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Farhan Sufyan Borhan said out of the total fatalities, 35 victims were children, with the highest figure of 14 deaths recorded in 2024.
He said department statistics showed 28 drowning fatalities in 2023, rising to 31 in 2024, then declining to 27 in 2025, with 10 so far this year.
For victims under 14, seven deaths were recorded in 2023, followed by 14 cases in 2024, 11 cases in 2025, and three cases so far this year.
Consequently, Farhan Sufyan said Kelantan JBPM is increasing preventive efforts through water safety education and awareness, including the free Program Jom Renang (Let’s Swim Programme) conducted in five series involving 300 children under 12 at various locations statewide.
“This programme aims to equip children with basic swimming skills, water safety knowledge, and self-rescue techniques as proactive steps to reduce the risk of drowning incidents,” he said.
He also reminded parents to constantly monitor their children near rivers, ponds, lakes, and open bodies of water, stressing that cooperation from schools, communities, and the public is vital to embedding water safety practices to avert drowning tragedies. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia calls for UN to challenge, abolish Security Council veto
Article:
NEW YORK, Sept 27 — The veto power of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) must be challenged and ultimately abolished to address the Council’s failures, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said expanding the Council’s membership alone would not be enough to resolve its shortcomings, stressing that the use of the veto must be questioned and strongly challenged by every member of the UN General Assembly, particularly in cases involving crimes against humanity.
“The exercise of the veto must be questioned and strongly challenged by every single member of this General Assembly. Particularly in cases of crimes against humanity,” he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st UN General Assembly here on Saturday.
Mohamad said Resolution 76/262 had already created an accountability channel between the Security Council and the General Assembly.
“We must make full use of this Resolution as a launchpad for greater accountability regarding the use of the veto,” he said.
He said the international community must begin work now to reform the Security Council.
“Expanding the Council’s membership alone will not be enough to resolve its failures. It is the veto that must be challenged, and it is the veto that must be abolished. We must begin the work now,” he said.
Mohamad said there was still time to save the global order, stressing that paralysis in the Security Council should not translate into paralysis of the United Nations.
He also highlighted the growing trust deficit confronting the UN, saying trust could only be restored through concrete action, including ensuring that international law was upheld and that people around the world continued to believe their voices mattered.
The UNSC is the United Nations’ principal body for addressing international peace and security, comprising 15 members, including five permanent members with veto power.
Mohamad is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 for Malaysia’s participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA). — Bernama

Title: ‘Malaysia will speak plainly: We are sick of it’: Mohamad Hasan tells UN to act on Gaza
Article:
NEW YORK, Sept 27 — The United Nations (UN) must move from reacting to crises to preventing them, with the task particularly urgent in Gaza, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.
He said the UN should not merely respond after disasters had occurred by counting the dead, delivering supplies and rebuilding what had been destroyed, only to wait for the next crisis.
“This cannot be the future of multilateralism. We must move from reaction to prevention,” he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st UN General Assembly here on Saturday.
Mohamad said nowhere was that task more urgent than in Gaza.
He said Malaysia and many other member states had exhausted every effort in the pursuit of justice for Gaza, including consistently calling for an immediate ceasefire and unrestricted supply of aid.
“We have supported humanitarian work in Palestine. We have pushed for punitive action towards Israel. And we have advocated for full Palestinian membership in this Hall,” he said.
However, he said the collective will of the General Assembly had repeatedly encountered the silencing effect of the veto.
“Malaysia will speak plainly: We are sick of it,” he said.
Mohamad said Malaysia would continue to support efforts to strengthen the multilateral system and ensure that it could respond effectively to conflicts and humanitarian crises.
According to Gaza’s Health Ministry, more than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed and over 174,000 injured in Gaza since October 2023.
The foreign minister is in New York from Sept 23 to 27 for Malaysia’s participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly (UNGA). — Bernama

Title: From trade fair to carnival, a look back at Pesta Pulau Pinang as its five-decade home makes way for LRT
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 27 — For the first time in over five decades, Pesta Pulau Pinang will not be held on the grounds Penangites have long called home.
The festival’s longtime site in Sungai Nibong has been closed to make way for construction of the Mutiara Line light rail transit (LRT) station and depot, forcing this year’s edition to relocate temporarily to Kubang Menerong in Tasek Gelugor.
December 2025 marked the last time Pesta was held at Sungai Nibong.
The site is also earmarked for a proposed Transit-Oriented Development Masterplan covering about 23.47 hectares — a long-term, mixed-use transit hub envisioned to take between 10 and 15 years to complete, incorporating residential, commercial and public facilities around an integrated transport network.
The plan does include a Pesta component, but on a smaller scale.
It’s a significant break from tradition for a festival that has anchored the earliest memories of generations of Penangites since the Sungai Nibong site first opened its doors in 1974.
Years before that permanent home was built, Pesta Pulau Pinang started as a commerce and tourism festival held in the inner city of George Town.
Pesta Pulau Pinang arch at Esplanade in 1966. — Picture courtesy of Laurence Bean
Penang was grappling with high unemployment and an uncertain investment climate following the loss of its free-port status in the late 1960s, so then-chief minister Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu introduced the festival as a way to stimulate retail activity.
The first Pesta Pulau Pinang was aimed at providing opportunities for traders while simultaneously promoting Penang as a tourist destination.
Interestingly, the late SM Mohamed Idris, widely known as the president of the Consumers Association of Penang, chaired the first Pesta organising committee.
The very first Pesta Pulau Pinang in 1966 showcased up to 100 traders with an emphasis on consumer products, business goods and industrial exhibits, and was held at Padang Kota Lama, or Esplanade.
The festival was also the year the Chingay procession was reintroduced, adding a carnival-like atmosphere to the event.
Processions were also held in conjunction with Pesta Pulau Pinang in 1971 before it shifted to its Sungai Nibong site. — Picture courtesy of Marcus Langdon Collection
Among those who visited the first Pesta in 1966 was Laurence Bean, who took some photos of his visit.
Though he could not remember much about that visit, he recalled being there on the same evening the Raja Permaisuri Agong was visiting the festival.
Pesta Pulau Pinang did not have a permanent site then, and was also held at Lebuh Macallum after the success of the first Pesta at Esplanade.
The state government eventually decided to build a dedicated Pesta site in Sungai Nibong, officially opened in 1974.
From there, Pesta began introducing a variety of programmes beyond the industrial and trade fair to draw crowds: open-air concerts, variety shows, food bazaars, exhibitions, pet shows, beauty pageants, film festivals and fashion shows, alongside traditional entertainment such as
joget
and
wayang kulit
, funfairs and sporting events including a go-kart prix.
A dragon boat race held in conjunction with Pesta used to take place off Gurney Drive.
Dragon boat race was held in conjunction with Pesta Pulau Pinang circa 1971. — Picture courtesy of Marcus Langdon Collection
The month-long festival became a huge draw, attracting visitors from other states as well as southern Thailand and Indonesia.
Held during the annual year-end school holiday, Pesta became a popular destination for Penangites and families to browse the trade fair for cheap bargains, eat at the food bazaar, or enjoy the rides, games and haunted house.
The 8.14-hectare site expanded over the years to include permanent stalls, performance arenas, parking areas, a
surau,
toilets, a miniature garden, automated teller machines and pavilions occupied by state agencies.
International pavilions representing Thailand, Aceh, North Sumatra and West Sumatra showcased food, clothing and other products from neighbouring territories.
Processions were also held in conjunction with Pesta Pulau Pinang in 1971 before it shifted to its Sungai Nibong site. — Picture courtesy of Marcus Langdon Collection
As visitors slowly diminished over the years due to new shopping centres and other forms of entertainment, Pesta evolved to keep drawing crowds — adding performances by Malaysian recording artistes, Battle of the Bands, cat shows,
silat
competitions,
muay thai
demonstrations, boxing matches, armed forces exhibitions, e-sports tournaments and mobile petting zoos.
The funfair remained one of its most recognisable components, with attractions such as the Euro Wheel, Vortex, Sky Rider, Daytona and roller coasters set against the brightly illuminated grounds.
Recent editions also featured
boria
performances, colouring competitions, Bollywood-themed programmes and nightly concerts, maintaining the festival’s mix of local culture and popular entertainment.
Throughout its evolution, the fair continued to provide a marketplace for small and medium enterprises, local traders and government agencies, preserving part of its original economic purpose even as entertainment became increasingly central to the event.
Pesta was cancelled only twice – in 2020 and 2021, due to the Covid-19 pandemic – before returning in 2022.
This year’s move to Tasek Gelugor marks its biggest disruption yet.

Title: Goh Sze Fei‑Nur Izzuddin storm into quarterfinals as Pearly Tan‑Thinaah sparkle with straight‑set wins
Article:
NAGOYA, Sept 26 — Malaysia’s national professional men’s doubles pair, Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, are one step away from securing a medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after advancing to the quarterfinals following a straight-set victory over Japan’s Yugo Kobayashi-Takuro Hoki today.
During the match held at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium, the national pair faced no major issues in claiming a 21-19, 21-16 straight-set win.
Waiting for the national pair in tomorrow’s quarterfinal round will be either China’s Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang or Thailand’s Chaloempoen Charoenkitamorn-Worrapol Thongsa-nga, who are set to play in another match later today.
Meanwhile, another national men’s doubles pair, Aaron Chia and Tee Kai Wun, fell short of reaching the quarterfinals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after bowing out to South Korea’s world number one pair, Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, in straight sets of 21-19, 21-16.
In the women’s doubles event, Pearly Tan-M Thinaah lived up to expectations by easily defeating Thailand’s Napapakorn Tungkasatan-Hathaihip 21-8, 21-12.
The national pair is scheduled to face India’s Gayatri Gopichand-Treesa Jolly, who pulled off an upset by defeating the host country’s pair 24-22, 21-18.
In the men’s singles event, national representative Justin Hoh failed to advance to the quarterfinals after losing to Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew 21-14, 21-14. — Bernama

Title: As heavy rain and flooding continue in Bangkok, Malaysians urged to stay vigilant
Article:
BANGKOK, Sept 26 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to exercise caution and remain vigilant as persistent heavy rain and flooding continue to disrupt roads and daily activities across the Thai capital, with all 50 districts declared disaster zones.
In an advisory issued Saturday, the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok urged Malaysians residing in or travelling to the city to keep abreast of the latest weather, road, and traffic conditions and plan their journeys in advance.
“Malaysians are advised to check road and flood conditions before travelling, allow additional travel time, avoid flood-affected areas, and consider alternative routes or modes of transport where necessary,” it said.
The embassy cautioned that weather and road conditions could change rapidly, particularly in flood-affected areas, and urged Malaysians to monitor local conditions and follow advisories and instructions issued by the relevant Thai authorities.
It said the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) provides an online Road Flood Monitoring System that allows the public to check road conditions and water levels at monitoring points across the capital.
The embassy said Malaysians could also report flooding or standing water through Traffy Fondue or contact the BMA Hotline at 1555, which operates around the clock.
For travel information, assistance or enquiries, Malaysians may contact the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) Contact Centre at 1672 or the Tourist Police at 1155.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt earlier declared all 50 districts in the capital disaster zones, following persistent heavy rain that caused flooding and traffic disruptions.
Flooding was reported in 93 districts, 350 sub-districts, and 1,425 villages, while waterlogging affected 44 road locations in Bangkok.
As of 7am on Saturday, flooding remained in 21 provinces nationwide, affecting 27,109 households and 84,605 people, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).
At press time, no casualties had been reported in Bangkok, although some e-hailing services had stopped accepting bookings due to road closures, while some shops remained closed. — Bernama

Title: Fama readies warehouses nationwide with buffer stocks as El Niño threat rises
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 26 — The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has taken proactive steps to safeguard the nation’s food supply by establishing a special committee two months ago to prepare for the possible impact of El Nino.
Its chairman, Abang Ahmad Kerdee Abang Masagus, said the move reflected Fama’s early action to prepare for the phenomenon, including plans to procure and store agro-food products at Fama warehouses nationwide.
“At Fama, we established a committee two months ago. Although El Niño is an annual phenomenon, we took proactive measures this year instead of waiting for it to occur.
“By taking early action and coordinating with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) on when the phenomenon is expected to begin, we were able to make early preparations this year,” he told reporters here today.
He said this when met at the Penang 2026 JAM Mega programme at Lotus’s Seberang Jaya, which was officiated by Penang State Rural Development, Agrotechnology, Food Security and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.
Previously, MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip was reported as saying that there was more than a 90 per cent probability of El Niño reaching the “very strong” or “Super El Nino” category between October and December.
Abang Ahmad Kerdee said Fama also planned to purchase selected agro-food products and keep them in its warehouses as buffer stocks against potential supply disruptions, including those caused by import and export issues.
He said Fama had warehouses in every state, including cold storage facilities, which would be fully utilised to ensure sufficient food supplies.
“The stocks include around 34 types of agro-food products, including red chillies, green chillies, cabbage and onions, as well as other food products such as chicken and beef.
“Should there be any issues, such as difficulties in securing imports or exports, we have a backup plan to ensure that there is sufficient supply of these products for several months,” he said.
Abang Ahmad Kerdee said the approach drew on the country’s experience during the Covid-19 pandemic, when early planning and adequate food stocks helped maintain continuity in food supplies. — Bernama

Title: Storm clouds gather: MetMalaysia issues urgent alert for Kuala Lumpur and 12 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 8pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Perlis, Terengganu, Kedah (Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Yan, Kuala Muda, Pendang, Padang Terap and Sik), as well as Penang (Seberang Perai Utara, Barat Daya and Timur Laut).
Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar and Manjung in Perak; Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Machang, Tanah Merah and Jeli in Kelantan.
Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pulau Tioman, Temerloh, Jerantut and Kuantan in Pahang; Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; Kuala Pilah, Tampin, Rembau and Jempol in Negeri Sembilan; and Mersing in Johor.
In Sabah and Sarawak, the affected areas are Sandakan, West Coast (Ranau, Kota Belud and Tuaran), Kudat (Kota Marudu), Tawau (Lahad Datu, Kalabakan and Kunak) and the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Sook, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut and Beaufort); and Limbang, Miri (Bario and Telang Usan), Kapit (Song, Belaga and Bukit Mabong), Sibu (Kanowit), Sarikei, Kuching, Serian (Tebedu), Betong (Saratok), Samarahan, and Sri Aman (Lubok Antu). — Bernama

Title: Madani Mart’s master licensing push could fuel 300 outlets, says Fuziah
Article:
KAJANG, Sept 26 — Madani Mart is opening master licensing applications to companies, investors, and strategic partners with financial and operational capabilities to accelerate its retail network expansion nationwide.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said each party appointed by Yayasan Madani will have the opportunity to develop and operate up to 100 Madani Mart branches, subject to set terms and standards.
“Currently, priority will be given to three (master licensees). This means if we appoint three, it will enable the opening of around 300 outlets,” she told Bernama after opening the Madani Mart Taman Sutera branch here today.
Fuziah, who is also Yayasan Madani chairman, said the appointment and branch development rights will be awarded in phases based on capability, performance, and compliance with the conditions established by Yayasan Madani.
She said expansion through this model will begin after Yayasan Madani ensures the supply chain and pricing for about 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs) offered by Madani Mart remain stable.
Fuziah said Yayasan Madani is negotiating with several commercial and government-owned banks to provide financing facilities up to RM50 million if required.
She added that the master licensing model was introduced to speed expansion. Opportunities to open individual outlets are still offered to ensure more entrepreneurs can join the network.
“We still want to provide opportunities to individual owners. We do not want a situation where only a select few make a profit,” she said, adding that Madani Mart aims to have at least one branch in every state legislative assembly constituency.
Meanwhile, on the opening of Madani Mart Taman Sutera, Fuziah said the third branch introduces a fresh grocery segment, including fish and vegetables, as well as bulk sales for items that do not require specific licences.
The bulk sales facility offers small traders, food operators, and stall owners options to obtain supplies in larger quantities at competitive prices, helping manage operating costs.
To date, Madani Mart operates two locations in Kuantan, Pahang, before opening in Taman Sutera, which marks the network’s first branch in the Klang Valley.
Madani Mart is a strategic partner of the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) in executing the Rahmah Madani Sales Programme (PJRM), with every outlet hosting at least one Rahmah Sale per month and providing payment system facilities for the Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) programme. — Bernama

Title: Van impaled by guardrail in Kuching crash, passenger injured
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 26 — A passenger van was impaled by a roadside guardrail after crashing at a traffic light junction in Bandar Baru Samariang this morning.
See Hua Daily News
reported that the incident occurred at about 7am today.
The van is believed to have lost control before crashing into the roadside barrier, causing the guardrail to pierce through the vehicle.
The van was carrying one female passenger at the time.
She sustained injuries in the incident and received initial treatment from paramedics at the scene before being taken to Sarawak General Hospital for further treatment. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar questions Opposition priorities: ‘No salary, they’re angry; those who steal, they don’t mention’
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned the federal Opposition’s priorities, taking a swipe at its MPs for scrutinising his refusal to draw a prime ministerial salary while, he said, saying little about those who “
sakau
”, or steal, large sums of money.
Anwar recalled being questioned by Opposition MPs in Parliament over how he could support himself without taking his salary as prime minister.
He said he had also been told by the Opposition that even Prophet Muhammad received wages, but added that he had never heard that the Prophet took a salary.
“Then I said, I don’t take a salary, but I don’t fall under the B40 category. Firstly, I take the allowance,” he said during a gathering with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni and students at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor.
Anwar said the government also provides the vehicle he uses, accommodation at the prime minister’s official residence, Seri Perdana, and flights.
“It’s enough
lah
. Not rich, but not poor,” he said of his financial position.
He then questioned what the Opposition had chosen to focus on.
“But they want to ‘
sibuk
’ [interfere], want to be angry. Don’t take a salary, they’re angry. Those who ‘
sakau
’ [steal] a lot, they don’t mention,” he said, drawing laughter from the audience.
Anwar did not elaborate on whom he was referring to in his remarks about the Opposition.
Last month, Anwar also used the word “
sakau
” when speaking about alleged past financial mismanagement at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the government’s July 29 release of a Royal Commission of Inquiry report into the pilgrims’ fund.
The RCI examined TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020. The government subsequently said investigations based on the report’s findings would proceed and that action would be taken if breaches of the law were established.
In 2024, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang reportedly suggested in the Dewan Rakyat that Anwar was seeking to appear more pious than Prophet Muhammad by refusing to accept a salary.
Anwar has declined to draw his salaries as prime minister and finance minister since taking office in November 2022, while continuing to receive his allowance as Tambun MP.

Title: PBS to reinforce unity and integrity while remaining in GRS, says president
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam wants the party to be strengthened as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven entity that remains relevant, while reaffirming its commitment to continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS).
He said the direction of the new PBS leadership would be based on three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today, ‘Unity, Stability, Integrity’.
“We may have different views and approaches, but our goal remains the same: to strengthen PBS and fight for Sabah’s future,” he said when delivering his presidential policy speech at the congress here.
He said the struggle concerning the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) was not yet over and PBS would continue to play an active role in defending Sabah’s rights and interests.
“This means our struggle is still a long one. PBS will continue to be an active, relevant and consistent voice in defending Sabah’s rights and interests. We do not want MA63 to merely become a political slogan; we want tangible implementation and results that the people can feel,” he said.
On unity, Dr Joachim said PBS needed to continue serving as a political home that united Sabahans regardless of race, religion, district or background.
He said the party would strengthen public participation by increasing the participation of Malays and Muslim Bumiputera, regaining the confidence of the Chinese community and providing greater opportunities for professionals, women and the younger generation.
“PBS does not belong to one race. PBS belongs to everyone who believes in the struggle for Sabah,” he said.
On GRS, he said PBS would continue to be a loyal, constructive and principled partner in the coalition.
Dr Joachim said PBS’ loyalty to the coalition did not mean that the party would lose its identity, but would continue to voice Sabah’s interests, including MA63, rural development, education, the economy, employment opportunities and the people’s well-being.
“We are with GRS, but we remain PBS. In terms of integrity, positions in PBS are not a gift but a trust that requires leaders to work, go to the ground, listen to the people’s problems and seek solutions,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kuala Pilah Form Two student death: Cause still undetermined after post-mortem, police question 21
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A post-mortem has failed to establish the cause of death of a 14-year-old boy whose death is being investigated following allegations of bullying at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police awaiting the results of further tests.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the examination was carried out at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Jaafar Hospital in Seremban from 10.30am today,
Harian
Metro
reported.
“The post-mortem, conducted by HTJ forensic pathologist Dr Akma Nurain Fairuz Mahamad Arif, was completed at 3pm today.
“The results of the post-mortem showed that the cause of death could not be determined at this time, and we are still awaiting the results of further tests,” Alzafny was quoted as saying.
He said police had so far recorded statements from 21 people, including students, teachers and the boy’s parents, as part of the investigation.
The student was found unconscious at the school hostel last night and was taken to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital in Kuala Pilah, where he was pronounced dead.
Police subsequently detained a 16-year-old student to assist in the investigation and opened an investigation paper under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The teenager was today remanded for six days, until October 1, to assist police with the investigation.
The Education Ministry has also ordered an immediate audit of the school following the boy’s death and said it would cooperate fully with police.

Title: Govt to announce firm measures to ensure fair wages in Budget 2027, says Anwar
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — The government will announce more decisive measures to ensure graduates secure jobs that match their qualifications and receive fair wages in Budget 2027, which will be tabled on October 9.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was currently at the final stage of preparing the budget and would formulate more concerted efforts to ensure that wage increases were commensurate with graduates’ qualifications.
“I have previously conducted a study on increases in productivity and wages. Take South Korea, for example, particularly where productivity is high, and wages have also increased accordingly.
“In Malaysia, productivity continues to increase, but wages have increased only slightly. So, we have to use the government’s authority to apply some pressure,” he said.
He said this when asked about the government’s measures to address the issue of fair wages commensurate with graduates’ qualifications during a question-and-answer session at the UiTM Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC) here today.
Asked about management issues and weaknesses at UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar said the matter needed to be studied before taking any action.
He said reports related to the matter would also be given attention through cooperation between the UiTM vice-chancellor, the Ministry of Higher Education and the Prime Minister’s Department.
“Please look into UiTM Holdings and find ways to work together with the vice-chancellor and the Prime Minister’s Department. My office will provide the necessary cooperation and input.
“Let’s not pass judgment now. Study the weaknesses first and rectify them, or change the people involved. We have changed dozens of agencies. But if there is indeed any wrongdoing, action must be taken,” he said.
Anwar said good governance was particularly important in Bumiputera agencies to ensure that they served as an example to society.
“I am stricter with Bumiputera agencies. That is right, because they should set an example,” he said.
In 2023, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigated allegations of misappropriation that resulted in losses of RM157 million incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The MACC investigation focused on several issues, particularly involving funds and several investments made by UiTM Holdings that resulted in losses amounting to millions of ringgit. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says he has not received Loke’s resignation letter
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to receive Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation letter.
“Wait for the resignation letter,” he said briefly when asked about Loke’s intention to resign from the Cabinet.
He spoke to reporters after attending the Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here today.
Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on September 19 in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
The Seremban MP said he would submit his resignation letter upon returning to Malaysia from China.
On the Registrar of Societies (RoS) order suspending all Perikatan Nasional (PN) activities in connection with the upcoming Melaka state election, Anwar said the matter should be referred to Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
RoS issued the suspension order, effective September 23, covering all PN activities.
According to RoS, the action was taken under Subsection 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966 following a notice issued to PN on September 22. — Bernama

Title: ‘Not a zero-sum game’: Anwar says he wants to help Malays, but not by denying others’ rights
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he wants to help Malays in the country, while stressing that this should not come at the expense of the rights of others because it is not a “zero-sum game”.
“But I’m confident the Bumiputera agenda can be expanded with a guarantee of social justice and without breaching the guarantee of safety and comfort of the non-Bumiputera.
“I always say, it’s not a zero-sum game. I want to help the Malays because they are my people. I’m proud of their culture, their heritage,” he said in a speech at Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here, drawing loud cheers from alumni and students.
“But I ‘
tidak senang
’ (dislike) any views that insult others, that belittle others’ roles or deny the rights of others. That is my stand,” he added.
Just before making the remarks, Anwar invited UiTM alumni to select seven to 10 representatives to evaluate programmes under Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM itself, and propose improvements.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar indicated that greater attention would be given to the socio-economic development of the Bumiputera community in next month’s federal Budget compared with previous Budgets.
He said this was not intended as divisive politics, but formed part of a national agenda, as the interests of the Bumiputera majority and indigenous communities in Sabah and Sarawak could not be sidelined.
Anwar also said he would be stricter in ensuring that every ringgit allocated to Malay and Bumiputera agencies was not misappropriated or subject to “
sakau
” (theft) by anyone, another remark that drew loud cheers from the audience.

Title: Khaled Nordin: Malaysia to reinforce defence, especially in Sabah, amid South China Sea tensions
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Malaysia needs to strengthen its national defence, particularly in Sabah, as a precaution in the event of a clash between major powers in the South China Sea.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia’s main concern was the possibility of a conflict or unexpected incident in the area that could have spillover effects on the country, particularly Sabah.
“If unexpected things happen, we know the challenges in the South China Sea and the rivalry between major powers. If something happens in that geographically small area, it could also affect our country,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled said this to reporters after the launch of the National Defence Literacy programme at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
He was commenting on concerns among Sabahans following defence cooperation between the Philippines and the United States (US), which has led to increased development of military bases, including on Balabac Island in Palawan, located about 50 kilometres from Banggi Island, Kudat, Sabah.
Mohamed Khaled said Malaysia respected the Philippines’ right to strengthen its defence capabilities through cooperation with the US, but the development needed to be given attention due to Sabah’s proximity to the country.
He said Malaysia did not dispute the Philippines’ move, but as a neighbouring country, any increase in the development of military bases or the presence of military assets in the area needed to be taken into account from the national security perspective.
“Every country has its own right to strengthen its national defence.
“That is their right, and we do not dispute it, but as a neighbouring country, we are paying attention and should take measures that can help our country in terms of defence,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Woman loses RM1.15m after falling for love scam syndicate in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 26 — A farmer and agricultural product trader lost more than RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual known as Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer.
“The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.
“After the victim made payments linked to the investment, the suspect introduced a platform called ‘Veniec Lottery,’ claimed to be an effort to recover the invested money,” he said in a statement today.
He said the victim was then persuaded to make several deposits to obtain profits and bonuses, before transferring funds to seven bank accounts totalling RM1,150,034.70, from her savings as well as loans from family members.
“However, the victim was unable to withdraw the money. Then she realised that she had been scammed,” he said. The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Azry Akmar advised the public not to be easily deceived by individuals who use friendship or special relationships to persuade them into making investments or handing over money.
“In addition, the public is advised to check account numbers and phone numbers through the Semak Mule platform before carrying out any financial transactions.
“Those who suspect they have become scam victims are urged to immediately contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 or lodge a police report,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says company losses are not a crime — fraud, abuse and ‘sakau’ are another matter
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Companies should not be penalised simply because they make losses, but action should be taken where there is fraud, abuse of power or “
sakau
”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Speaking after addressing issues including the scrutiny of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Anwar said companies could go through periods of losses as well as profits, and that losses alone should not be grounds for punishment.
“We don’t ‘
hukum
’ (punish) people because a company makes losses. We ‘
hukum
’ because there is fraud, there is abuse of power, there is ‘
sakau
’ (stealing), not because of losses,” he said during a question-and-answer session with Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) alumni and students at UiTM’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor here.
Turning to UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar cautioned against passing judgment before its position had been properly examined.
“Now study UiTM Holdings, don’t ‘
hukum
’ (pass judgment) now,” he said, adding that any weaknesses should first be identified and improved, but action should be taken if abuses were found.
Earlier, a member of the audience asked Anwar whether he could direct the Higher Education Ministry or UiTM alumni to produce a report on UiTM Holdings, which the questioner claimed had accumulated more than RM100 million in unresolved losses.
Anwar indicated that the Higher Education Ministry would be involved, adding that the Prime Minister’s Department would cooperate. He also thanked UiTM’s vice-chancellor for giving full cooperation over the UiTM Holdings issue.
During the dialogue, Anwar also addressed the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, saying it had been completed before he became prime minister in 2022 amid questions over why it was only released this year.
He said the report’s release had been delayed after TH’s leadership asked for more time, amid concerns that depositors could withdraw their savings if it was made public earlier.
Anwar rejected suggestions that the report had been released as an act of “revenge”, saying decisions over investigations, prosecutions and judgments rested with the relevant authorities.
“I don’t know who is being investigated, whether they will be charged or whether action will be taken. The investigation is handled by investigating bodies — the police, the Inland Revenue Board, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission; deciding whether to charge is under the attorney general, and judges make the decisions.
“But to say we are acting out of ‘
dendam
’ (revenge), that’s not true,” he said.
Anwar also said issues involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), which is currently under scrutiny, predated his tenure as prime minister.
He said he was particularly strict about governance at Bumiputera agencies, which he said should set an example not only for Muslims but for society as a whole.

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across much of Malaysia until this evening
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across the country, except Sarawak, until 5pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect the whole of Perlis and Penang.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they comprise Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak.
The warning also covers Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kuala Krai in Kelantan, as well as Besut, Hulu Terengganu and Dungun in Terengganu.
In Pahang, the areas involved are Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor and Klang.
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau and Kuala Pilah, while in Johor, they are Tangkak, Muar, Batu Pahat and Mersing.
In Sabah, the warning covers Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Paitan and Sandakan), Tawau (Lahad Datu and Kunak), the West Coast, Interior (Membakut, Tambunan, Keningau, Sipitang, Beaufort and Tenom) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: Mindef launches national defence literacy drive to prepare public for new security threats
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) today launched the National Defence Literacy Programme to boost the public’s awareness, knowledge and understanding of national defence, security and sovereignty.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a shifting security threat landscape demands a deeper understanding of national defence, and a recognition of the role Malaysians can play in safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty.
“This is where what we call defence literacy comes in. It is an awareness, a body of knowledge and a skill that every citizen must possess,” he told reporters after launching the National Defence Literacy Programme at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and Army chief Jen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman.
Others in attendance were MiDAS chief executive Laksdya Datuk Yusne Mokhtar, Office of Home Affairs and Research secretary Datuk Awang Shaminan Awang Ashaari, and Sabah National Security Council director Datuk Yahya Sulaiman.
Mohamed Khaled said the public must grasp the fact that security threats today are far more complex. They are no longer confined to physical or military danger, but are alive in the digital space too.
“That is exactly why we are running this Literacy Programme. We want to build the people’s resilience. When the people are resilient, it becomes a deterrent force,” he said.
He said defence literacy efforts must be sustained, so the public not only understands defence and security issues better, but also sees the role they can play in contributing to national defence. Sabah was picked as the first state to roll out the programme, before it is expanded nationwide.
Earlier in his speech, Mohamed Khaled framed national defence through three key components: defence as the nation’s fence or shield, defence as the nation’s umbrella, and defence as the anchor or pillar of a sovereign nation.
He said the defence literacy agenda is about showing the public that there are many ways to strengthen the people’s resilience.
“Ways that don’t require anyone to become a soldier or take up arms,” he said, adding that a range of awareness programmes on defence issues will be rolled out actively.
“We want the public to understand one thing clearly: defence issues no longer start with an enemy at our borders or waters. Threats to sovereignty are everywhere,” he said.
The one-day programme featured two headline segments:
Bicara Ancaman Kognitif
(Talk on Cognitive Threats) and
Bicara Pahlawan Negara
(Talk on National Warriors). They zeroed in on how threats now target public thought and perception in today’s security landscape.
The
Bicara Pahlawan Negara
session brought together Major General (Rtd) Datuk Dr Radzi Abd Hamid as moderator and four special panellists: Lieutenant General (Rtd) Datuk Seri Zain Mohd Said SP, Major General Datuk Mohd Halim Khalid PGB, Warrant Officer 1 (Rtd) Freaddey Yojod and Lance Corporal (Rtd) Abdul Rahman Maidin.
The National Defence Literacy Programme is a Mindef initiative led by the Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security (MiDAS) in collaboration with Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia.
At its core, it aims to sharpen public awareness of one simple truth: every layer of society has a role in defending the nation’s security and sovereignty. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: UiTM Jalan Othman Campus renamed in honour of Arshad Ayub, architect of institution’s early growth
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Jalan Othman Campus in Petaling Jaya has been renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman Campus in recognition of the late educationist’s contributions to the development of the institution.
Anwar said the renaming was a tribute to Arshad’s legacy, having played a key role in the development of the Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM) into UiTM, while also being known for his firm emphasis on educational quality, good governance and expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students.
He described Arshad as a highly respected Malay educationist who was firm and uncompromising, particularly when it came to education, quality and opportunities for Malay students.
Anwar said Arshad had also maintained a strong commitment to governance and institutional integrity, rather than using Malay institutions or agencies for personal gain or allowing them to be undermined by misconduct.
“Today’s younger generation may not remember him, but as times change, many have emerged claiming to be champions of the Malay cause and speaking about the struggle for the Malays. However, not many have maintained the same commitment to good governance or refrained from using Malay institutions and agencies to enrich themselves or undermine them,” he said.
Anwar said Arshad’s legacy should therefore be viewed not only in terms of his role in establishing and strengthening the institution, but also in the way he managed it and upheld good governance, which he said contributed to the growth of ITM’s Jalan Othman campus.
He was speaking at the UiTM Alumni Gathering with the Prime Minister at the university’s Dewan Agung Tuanku Canselor (DATC) here today.
Also present at the gathering were Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abdul Halim, UiTM Vice-Chancellor Prof Datuk Dr Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin and Universiti Teknologi MARA Alumni Federation of Malaysia (PAUiTM) President Saiful Azhar Shaharun.
The late Arshad, who died in 2022, was the first director of ITM, serving from 1967 to 1975 before it became known as UiTM. He was regarded as a driving force behind the development of education at ITM and had also served as a ministry secretary-general.
As an immediate measure, Anwar also approved RM2.5 million to upgrade the campus.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government would continue to prioritise the Bumiputera development agenda, including strengthening Bumiputera educational institutions and agencies, in line with the principle of social justice.
At the same time, he stressed that efforts to strengthen the Bumiputera agenda should not come at the expense of the rights and interests of the non-Bumiputera community.
“There are people who ask about the Madani Government’s attitude and position on the Bumiputera agenda. We hear it in the political discourse, sometimes through insinuations and suggestions that we are sidelining it.
“I want to give you the figures. For example, the operating and development allocation for UiTM alone, which was less than RM2 billion before the Madani Government, has increased every year. The allocation for UiTM in 2026 is RM3.08 billion.
“And now, as we approach the final weeks before the national Budget is announced on Oct 9, I want to give an assurance that our commitment to the Bumiputera development agenda and Bumiputera agencies will continue to receive attention.
“I want to demonstrate that under the Madani Government, the attention given to the development and economic, social and educational advancement of the Bumiputera is far greater than under any previous administration,” he said.
Anwar also urged UiTM alumni to play a greater role in helping the government assess and strengthen major programmes of Bumiputera agencies, particularly UiTM.
He proposed that PAUiTM select between seven and 10 alumni to evaluate the programmes, including providing views on new fields of study that should be expanded, such as artificial intelligence (AI), quantum computing and healthcare.
“I will provide every opportunity and avenue for you to evaluate each major programme of Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM, so that they can be improved and enhanced,” he said.
The prime minister also stressed the importance of student welfare, particularly for those from low-income families, including ensuring that no student faces food insecurity while pursuing their studies.
As a gesture of support and appreciation for PAUiTM’s efforts, the Prime Minister approved RM100,000 each for two programmes — the TUNaS Belia NEET Programme and the UiTM Alumni Fellowship Gathering. — Bernama

Title: Akmal Nasrullah: Removing 30pc Bumiputera equity rule for private education will not weaken empowerment agenda
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Sept 26 — The removal of the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for private education institutions (IPS) will not undermine the government’s agenda to empower the community, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said implementation and follow-up measures arising from the removal of the requirement would be handled by the relevant ministries according to their respective jurisdictions.
Akmal Nasrullah said the Bumiputera empowerment agenda should instead be viewed in terms of strengthening the community’s capacity to participate in and expand its presence in the economy.
“The government will continue to strengthen the Bumiputera empowerment agenda through approaches that can increase their capacity to continue growing and participating in economic activities,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after attending the closing ceremony of the Rehda Institute Youth Initiative (RIYI) 2026 here.
Akmal Nasrullah said the government remained focused on increasing Bumiputera participation and capabilities in economic activities, and that removing the equity requirement did not signal any reduction in its commitment to the community’s economic empowerment.
At the event, the minister was also presented with the RIYI 2026 closing summary report, which highlighted a gap between students’ expectations and employers’ assessments of graduates’ workplace readiness.
The survey found that 41.6 per cent of student respondents considered one to three months a realistic period for fresh graduates to begin adding commercial value at work, compared with just 2.9 per cent of employers who held the same view.
Meanwhile, 62 per cent of students said they felt adequately prepared by their universities, while only 32.3 per cent of employers agreed that local universities sufficiently prepared graduates for workplace realities.
The survey involved students and recent graduates from 21 Malaysian universities as well as employers, although the report cautioned that the findings came from targeted surveys and were not nationally representative.
The report also highlighted the growing impact of artificial intelligence on entry-level employment. Some 76.4 per cent of student respondents said they regularly used AI tools, while half of the employers surveyed expected AI to reduce the number of entry-level positions they would hire for over the next three years.
On career development, 79.4 per cent of employers said they were willing to provide structured training and a clear career path in return for a commitment from employees to stay, while 67.6 per cent of students said they would accept such an arrangement.
The survey also found that 82.4 per cent of students and 58.3 per cent of employers supported compulsory salary-range disclosure in job advertisements, while 57.1 per cent of students said they were likely or very likely to work outside Malaysia within five years.
The findings form part of RIYI 2026’s focus on narrowing the gap between universities and industry, with the initiative bringing students together with industry leaders to gain exposure to workplace expectations, career development and the skills needed in a technology-driven economy.
Rehda Institute chairman Datuk Jeffrey Ng Tiong Lip said closer collaboration between universities and industry was needed to give students earlier exposure to workplace realities.
“A university qualification provides an important foundation, but young people also need to understand how workplaces operate, how decisions are made and what employers expect from them.
“This is where RIYI plays an important role in bringing students closer to industry through direct engagement and mentorship, while helping them develop the judgement, resilience, communication and adaptability needed to build sustainable careers,” he said.
The RIYI 2026 programme brought together students from more than 21 universities, with its final session focusing on AI’s impact on junior roles, productivity, decision-making and the capabilities expected of future leaders.

Title: Sarawak to set up authority to manage and develop lakes, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 26 — Sarawak will establish an authority to oversee, manage and develop the state’s lake areas in a comprehensive manner.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the initiative is part of the state’s development plans for the next five years.
He said the plans took into account approaches adopted by other states to develop lake areas as resort destinations while providing better facilities.
“Insya-Allah, we will establish an authority to oversee all our lakes in Sarawak, including rivers with potential,” he said at the launch of the Sarawakku Sayang 2026 programme in Betong today.
Abang Johari said the initiative was also expected to add value to the state’s economic growth while further strengthening Sarawak’s existing strengths.
Meanwhile, he said the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak (CENTEXS) would establish a Flying School Academy in Betong to support the state’s efforts to advance modern agriculture through drone technology.
“Drones are important, in addition to aircraft, which is why I support the establishment of a flying academy here in collaboration with the private sector.
“This is because licences are required, while the open airspace here provides a conducive environment for students to learn how to operate drones in the Betong area,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kuskop channels nearly RM10b to 270,000 entrepreneurs as of August, seeks bigger Budget 2027 allocation, says minister
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 26 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) has channelled nearly RM10 billion through various support and financing programmes under the ‘Power Up 10K’ initiative to about 270,000 entrepreneurs nationwide as of the end of August.
Its minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the achievement was among the reasons Kuskop had proposed to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) for larger allocations for the micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and cooperative sectors under Budget 2027.
“The RM10 billion is part of the RM15 billion target to be channelled to the MSME and cooperative sectors this year. In Penang alone, RM760 million was channelled in the first eight months, benefiting about 6,000 entrepreneurs.
“If Malaysians want to do business in Malaysia but do not have opportunities, let us not talk about overseas markets first. We must ensure Malaysian businesses, products and services can penetrate the domestic market before going abroad,” he told reporters after the 2026 “
Hebatkan Perniagaan Malaysia
” (HPM) Carnival, Penang edition, at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Sim noted that financing support for the MSME sector had been increased to RM60 billion this year from RM50 billion previously.
He said Kuskop had also proposed reducing the cost of doing business and improving government delivery efficiency to help MSMEs expand. Measures included simplifying government processes, shortening processing times and reducing related fees and charges.
“If we cannot control global oil prices, at least we can control local costs. Government processes must be made easier and processing times, fees and charges, including taxes where possible, should be reduced so that MSMEs can have some breathing space,” he said.
Sim advised that delays in obtaining licences, permits or financing could cause entrepreneurs to lose business opportunities. He added that Kuskop, through Tekun Nasional, had reduced the financing application period to seven days from 30 to 40 days previously, while financing below RM20,000 must be approved within 24 hours.
“The principles Kuskop has conveyed to MOF are, firstly, more funding for the MSME and cooperative sectors; secondly, a lower cost of doing business; and thirdly, greater government delivery efficiency,” he said. — Bernama
